prompt: For the data set $2$, $4$, $4$, $5$, $10$, which statement is true?

choices.label: The mean is greater than the median
The median is greater than the mean
The mean and median are equal
The mean is less than the smallest value

hint: Look at how the values are spread. One value is much larger than the others, and that affects one of the two measures more.

hints.text: Look at how the values are spread. One value is much larger than the others, and that affects one of the two measures more.
The list is already sorted, so the median is the third value. For the mean, add the five values to get $25$ and divide by $5$.
The mean is $5$ and the median is $4$, so the mean is greater than the median, which is choice A.

learningObjective: Compare mean and median for a skewed data set.
explanation: The values are already in order, so the median is the third of the five values, which is $4$.
The mean is the sum divided by the count: $\dfrac{2 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 10}{5} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5$.
The value $10$ lies far above the rest and pulls the mean up, while the median does not move.
Since $5$ is greater than $4$, the mean is greater than the median, which is choice A.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the skew instead of computing
steps: The values cluster at $2$-$5$ with one straggler at $10$ — right-skewed.
The mean chases outliers; the median ignores them. So in a right-skewed set, mean > median.
Left-skewed reverses it. Knowing this rule answers most center-comparison questions without any arithmetic.
